# Stripe → Mailchimp Connector

Adds a customer to a Mailchimp audience with their Stripe plan as a tag when a `payment_intent.succeeded` webhook is received.

## What it does

1. Receives a Stripe `payment_intent.succeeded` webhook payload.
2. Validates the payload structure and event type.
3. Extracts the customer email and subscription plan ID.
4. Calls the Mailchimp API to add/update a subscriber in the configured audience with the plan as a tag.

## Configuration

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |
|-----------------|----------------------|-------------|
| `stripeWebhookSecret` | `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Stripe webhook signing secret (used by the platform to verify the `Stripe-Signature` header before invoking the connector). |
| `mailchimpApiKey` | `MAILCHIMP_API_KEY` | Mailchimp API key (used as Bearer token). |
| `mailchimpListId` | `MAILCHIMP_LIST_ID` | The Mailchimp audience/list ID (appears in the URL path). |
| `fetch` | — | Optional injected `fetch` implementation for testing or custom HTTP clients. |

## Usage Example

```typescript
import { handle, ConnectorConfig } from './connector';

const config: ConnectorConfig = {
  stripeWebhookSecret: process.env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
  mailchimpApiKey: process.env.MAILCHIMP_API_KEY!,
  mailchimpListId: process.env.MAILCHIMP_LIST_ID!,
};

// In your webhook handler (after platform verifies Stripe-Signature):
const result = await handle(stripeWebhookPayload, config);
console.log('Mailchimp member ID:', result.mailchimpMemberId);
```

## Assumptions

- The Stripe webhook payload includes a `customer` object with an `email` field and a `subscription` object with a `plan.id` field. If these are not expanded (i.e., they are string IDs), the connector falls back to using the customer ID as a synthetic email (`{customer_id}@stripe.local`) and the subscription ID as the tag.
- The Mailchimp audience already exists and accepts tags on subscriber records.
- The plan identifier from Stripe can be directly used as a Mailchimp tag (no additional mapping required).
- The platform (or upstream middleware) verifies the `Stripe-Signature` header using `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` before calling this connector. The connector itself does not perform signature verification.
- Mailchimp API endpoint uses the `us1` region (`https://us1.api.mailchimp.com`). Adjust the connector if your account uses a different data center.

export function fakeFetch(

    calls.push(call)
    return handler(call)

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */

}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}

export interface ConnectorConfig {
  /** Intercom webhook secret (client_secret) used to verify X-Hub-Signature header. */
  intercomWebhookSecret: string;
  /** Zendesk OAuth access token for Bearer authentication. */
  zendeskAccessToken: string;
  /** Zendesk subdomain (e.g., 'mycompany' for mycompany.zendesk.com). */
  zendeskSubdomain: string;
  /** Optional fetch implementation for testing. */
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
}

export interface IntercomWebhookPayload {
  type: string;
  topic: string;
  data: {
    item: {
      type: string;
      id: string;
      url: string;
    };
  };
}

export interface HandleResult {
  ticketId: number;
  ticketUrl: string;
}

export async function handle(payload: IntercomWebhookPayload, config: ConnectorConfig): Promise<HandleResult> {
  // Validate input
  if (!payload || typeof payload !== 'object') {
    throw new Error('Invalid payload: expected an object');
  }
  if (payload.topic !== 'conversation_part.tag.created') {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported topic: ${payload.topic}. Expected 'conversation_part.tag.created'`);
  }
  if (!payload.data?.item) {
    throw new Error('Missing data.item in payload');
  }
  const { id, url, type: itemType } = payload.data.item;
  if (!id) {
    throw new Error('Missing conversation id in payload.data.item');
  }
  if (!url) {
    throw new Error('Missing conversation url in payload.data.item');
  }
  if (itemType !== 'conversation') {
    throw new Error(`Unsupported item type: ${itemType}. Expected 'conversation'`);
  }

  // Prepare Zendesk ticket
  const ticketSubject = id;
  const ticketCommentBody = `Conversation URL: ${url}`;

  const zendeskUrl = `https://${config.zendeskSubdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/tickets.json`;
  const requestBody = {
    ticket: {
      subject: ticketSubject,
      comment: {
        body: ticketCommentBody,
      },
    },
  };

  const fetchImpl = config.fetch ?? fetch;
  const response = await fetchImpl(zendeskUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${config.zendeskAccessToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(requestBody),
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    const errorText = await response.text().catch(() => '');
    throw new Error(`Zendesk API error: ${response.status} ${response.statusText} for POST ${zendeskUrl} - ${errorText}`);
  }

  const result = (await response.json()) as { ticket: { id: number; url: string } };
  // Replace any {subdomain} placeholder in the returned URL with the actual subdomain
  const normalizedUrl = result.ticket.url.replace('{subdomain}', config.zendeskSubdomain);
  return {
    ticketId: result.ticket.id,
    ticketUrl: normalizedUrl,
  };
}

Creates a Zendesk ticket when an Intercom conversation receives the `refund` tag. The ticket includes a link back to the Intercom conversation.

3. Calls the Zendesk Tickets API (`POST /api/v2/tickets.json`) to create a ticket:

   - **First comment body**: `Conversation URL: <intercom_conversation_url>`
4. Returns the created Zendesk ticket ID and URL.

## Configuration / Environment Variables

| Config Property | Environment Variable | Description |

const STATUS_TEXT: Record<number, string> = {
  200: 'OK', 201: 'Created', 202: 'Accepted', 204: 'No Content',
  400: 'Bad Request', 401: 'Unauthorized', 403: 'Forbidden', 404: 'Not Found', 409: 'Conflict',
  422: 'Unprocessable Entity', 429: 'Too Many Requests',
  500: 'Internal Server Error', 502: 'Bad Gateway', 503: 'Service Unavailable',
}

/** A JSON Response with the standard status text, e.g. jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 401) -> "401 Unauthorized". */
export function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status = 200): Response {
  const init = { status, statusText: STATUS_TEXT[status] ?? '', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }
  return new Response(status === 204 ? null : JSON.stringify(body), init)
}

function parseJson(raw: string | undefined): unknown {
  if (raw === undefined) return undefined
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function urlMatches(template: string, actual: string): boolean {
  const t = splitUrl(template)
  const a = splitUrl(actual)
  if (!t || !a) return false
  const tHost = t.host.split('.')
  const aHost = a.host.split('.')
  if (tHost.slice(-2).join('.') !== aHost.slice(-2).join('.')) return false
  const tPath = t.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  const aPath = a.path.replace(/\/+$/, '').split('/')
  if (tPath.length !== aPath.length) return false
  return tPath.every((segment, i) => isPlaceholder(segment) || segment === aPath[i])
}

function splitUrl(url: string): { host: string; path: string } | null {
  const match = url.match(/^https?:\/\/([^/?#]+)([^?#]*)/i)
  return match ? { host: (match[1] ?? '').toLowerCase(), path: match[2] || '/' } : null
}

function isPlaceholder(segment: string): boolean {
  return /^\{[^}]+\}$|^:[A-Za-z_]\w*$|^<[^>]+>$/.test(segment)
}
